name: BR (Bendamustine + Rituximab)

institution.provenance: DRAFT decision-support protocol authored from standard-of-care dosing (experimental; owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

premedications.name: Rituximab infusion-reaction prophylaxis
premedications.notes: antihistamine, antipyretic and (per practice) a corticosteroid before the infusion.

premedications.name: Tumor-lysis-syndrome prophylaxis
premedications.notes: hydration and allopurinol for higher tumor burden.

supportiveCare: A gentler chemoimmunotherapy option than FCR for older or less-fit, TP53 wild-type patients; never use with del(17p)/TP53 mutation.
PJP and herpesvirus (VZV/HSV) prophylaxis per risk.
Hepatitis B reactivation prophylaxis if HBcAb-positive (anti-CD20 antibody).
The 90 mg/m2 bendamustine dose is used first-line; a reduced 70 mg/m2 is often used in the relapsed/refractory setting.
monitoring: CBC with differential before each cycle
renal and liver function before each cycle
skin review (bendamustine cutaneous reactions) and infection surveillance

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 cytopenia or significant renal/hepatic impairment
doseModificationRules.text: Delay or reduce bendamustine for significant cytopenia or organ impairment per standard practice; physician decides.

drugs.name: Bendamustine
drugs.notes: Standard dosing (NCCN / DeVita, general reference): 90 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 2 of a 28-day cycle for up to 6 cycles as first-line CLL therapy; a reduced 70 mg/m2 is commonly used for relapsed/refractory disease. Own wording; not copied from any source.

drugs.name: Rituximab
drugs.notes: Standard dosing (NCCN / DeVita, general reference): 375 mg/m2 IV on day 1 of cycle 1, then 500 mg/m2 IV on day 1 of cycles 2 through 6. dosePerUnit is the first-cycle 375 mg/m2 dose; the 500 mg/m2 escalation from cycle 2 is noted here. Own wording; not copied from any source.
